title: ServiceNow Invests $40 Million in India's BusinessNext at $700 Million Valuation
excerpt: The strategic deal gives the Noida-based banking software firm access to ServiceNow's global sales network as it pushes into AI-powered autonomous banking.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • ServiceNow invested $40 million in BusinessNext, valuing it at $700 million, a significant increase from 2021.
  • BusinessNext aims to enhance its AI banking platform and expand into Australia and New Zealand with the new capital.
  • The partnership will integrate ServiceNow's AI Control Tower with BusinessNext's platform for over 120 global financial institutions.
  • BusinessNext reported $32 million in revenue for FY25, with half coming from international markets.
ServiceNow's Strategic Investment
›ServiceNow's investment: $40 million
›BusinessNext's valuation: $700 million
›Previous valuation in 2021: $181 million
›Stake acquired: ~5%

ServiceNow has invested $40 million in BusinessNext, an Indian banking software company, valuing the Noida-based firm at $700 million and acquiring a roughly 5% stake. The deal marks a nearly fourfold increase from BusinessNext's last reported valuation of $181 million in 2021 and is the largest investment ServiceNow Ventures has made in an Indian company.

https://x.com/Techmeme/status/2080217763138941001

The investment positions the two companies to jointly sell AI-powered banking software to financial institutions worldwide. BusinessNext will deploy the capital to strengthen its autonomous banking platform, build out private AI capabilities for regulated financial institutions, and expand into Australia and New Zealand.

"Think of it as a strategic partnership, which is cemented with funding."

— Nishant Singh, Founder and CEO, BusinessNext

From CRM Vendor to Autonomous Banking Platform

Founded in 2001 by Nishant Singh and Bidhan Chaudhary, BusinessNext — formerly known as CRMNext until it rebranded in 2022 — has spent more than two decades building software for banks and financial institutions. The company now serves over 120 institutions globally, including the Reserve Bank of India, State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, and Arab Bank.

Its platform is used by more than one million bankers across 75,000-plus branches, reaching over one billion end customers globally, according to the company. BusinessNext's AI agents automate tasks such as loan processing, document verification, approval routing, customer follow-ups, and compliance checks.

"We actually renamed our company and we kind of rewrote our stack to put that fundamentally at the core," Singh told TechCrunch, describing how AI was built into the platform from the outset rather than bolted on afterward.

Why ServiceNow Over Traditional Investors

Singh said BusinessNext chose ServiceNow over potential financial investors to accelerate its international expansion by tapping into the U.S. software giant's global sales infrastructure. The partnership would help BusinessNext "borrow" ServiceNow's go-to-market "machinery" in markets where the Indian company has limited presence, he said.

The deal extends beyond capital. As part of the partnership, BusinessNext will integrate ServiceNow's AI platform, including its AI Control Tower, with its own products to help banks deploy and manage AI agents while maintaining governance and observability.

"India's financial services sector is at an inflection point — institutions are moving from digital experimentation to full-scale AI-led operations."

— Kulmeet Bawa, Group VP and MD for India and SAARC, ServiceNow

Profitable and Growing

BusinessNext is one of a relatively small number of Indian SaaS startups that have reached profitability. The company reported operating revenue of ₹265.3 crore (approximately $32 million) in FY25, up from ₹256.8 crore in FY24, according to financial data cited by Inc42. It posted a net profit of ₹4.6 crore during the year, swinging from a net loss of ₹14.7 crore the previous year.

About half of BusinessNext's revenue now comes from outside India, with overseas markets expected to drive much of its future growth. The company employs more than 1,300 people and has raised over $60 million in total external funding from investors including Avataar Ventures, Norwest Venture Partners, and Ascent Capital.

Competitive Landscape and What's Next

BusinessNext competes with major enterprise vendors including Salesforce Financial Services Cloud, Microsoft Dynamics 365, FIS, Temenos, and Pegasystems in the banking technology market. The ServiceNow partnership could sharpen its competitive edge in the U.S., Southeast Asia, Australia, and New Zealand — markets where Singh said the company aims to grow aggressively.

The deal reflects broader investor appetite for AI-native enterprise software companies serving regulated sectors. Several Indian SaaS startups, including Freshworks, Whatfix, and Perfios, have also been expanding their AI capabilities to automate enterprise workflows. For Indian-origin professionals across the global banking and technology sectors, BusinessNext's trajectory underscores how India's enterprise software industry is increasingly producing companies with global product-led ambitions rather than services-only models.
